name: Dinosaur Jr.
label: SST
lede: Three kids from western Massachusetts got banned from almost every club in town for volume, sued over their own name, and split so badly the bassist wrote songs about it for a decade, then came back and outlasted everyone.

hero.by: Photo: Wikimedia Commons (Le Trabendo, Paris, October 2022)

eras.title: Deep Wound, then a one-show band called Mogo
eras.text: J Mascis and Lou Barlow met as hardcore kids in Amherst, with Mascis on drums. When hardcore got too narrow, Mascis switched to guitar and wrote songs that stunned Barlow, then quietly fired his first singer after one night.

years.h: J Mascis drums, Lou Barlow plays guitar in [[Deep Wound|7cee4e5d-8ea4-48fb-a7e2-c3adcc543f81]]
years.p: Barlow's high school hardcore band gets its drummer when [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]] answers an ad for someone who could play really fast.

years.h: Deep Wound breaks up; J Mascis moves to guitar
years.p: Mascis starts writing his own songs and asks [[Lou Barlow|6523f86d-11d3-489e-81f6-6cbe08c367de]] to play bass. Barlow later called the songs brilliant, far beyond his own.

years.cap: Dinosaur Jr. at the Ritz, Manchester, 2013 · Wikimedia
years.h: First show as Mogo ends with an anti-police rant
years.p: Mascis, Barlow, drummer [[Murph|9d47f849-23c5-4a9f-88eb-db2774595bf8]] and singer Charlie Nakajima play the UMass Amherst campus. Nakajima launches into an onstage tirade against the police, and Mascis breaks up Mogo the next day.
years.xp: Mascis admitted he was too wimpy to fire Nakajima outright. He re-formed the band with Barlow and Murph and simply didn't tell Nakajima. The new trio called itself Dinosaur, with Mascis and Barlow splitting lead vocals.

eras.title: Too loud for Amherst
eras.text: Dinosaur played so loud that people left rooms and clubs stopped booking them. Sonic Youth heard it differently, took them on tour, and helped move them from Homestead to SST, where the band made two records that pointed straight at grunge.

years.h: Dinosaur, made for $500 on Homestead
years.p: Recorded at a home studio outside Northampton. It sold around 1,500 copies in its first year and got almost no press; Barlow sings many leads because J Mascis wasn't comfortable singing yet.

years.h: Banned from nearly every club around Amherst
years.p: In a SPIN oral history, Murph recalled Dinosaur getting banned from nearly every club around Amherst and Northampton except one. People left rooms to get away from the volume.

years.h: [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] take Dinosaur on the road
years.p: Unimpressed at first, Sonic Youth saw Dinosaur several times, became fans, and invited them on a tour across the Northeast and Midwest.

years.h: J Mascis picks SST over Homestead
years.p: Homestead's [[Gerard Cosloy|b3c600d5-e1dd-4525-855d-6d4f950c3be6]] felt betrayed when Mascis skipped a two-album Homestead deal to go to [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]]'s SST. Mascis then moved to New York, and Barlow and Murph felt left behind.

years.h: You're Living All Over Me, SST No. 130
years.p: Engineered by [[Wharton Tiers|de3636ee-5022-462b-b427-34be9674f281]] in New York. J Mascis dictated Murph's every drumbeat; Barlow got two songs, Lose and Poledo, the second sung over his ukulele.
years.xp:
Mascis's own favorite Dinosaur Jr. album. Pitchfork put it at No. 40 on its 1980s list and it has been called the first perfect indie rock album.

Barlow on the sessions: Murph could not handle how tightly Mascis controlled his parts.

years.h: Sixties veterans force the name Dinosaur Jr.
years.p: Dinosaurs, a supergroup of ex-members of the Grateful Dead, Jefferson Airplane, Quicksilver and Country Joe and the Fish, sent a cease and desist. SST recalled early copies of the new LP credited to Dinosaur.
years.xp: Dinosaurs included [[Robert Hunter|e9b419b5-ab8f-425c-8214-a7259e6efe10]], Spencer Dryden, Peter Albin, John Cipollina and Barry Melton. They had formed in California in 1982 and broke up in 1989. SST reprinted You're Living All Over Me with the corrected name.

years.src: Our Band Could Be Your Life via Dangerous Minds · Magnet
years.h: J Mascis hits Lou Barlow with his guitar onstage
years.p: At a Connecticut club, Barlow makes bass feedback instead of playing his parts. Mascis crosses the stage, hits him repeatedly with his guitar and storms off.
years.xp: In Michael Azerrad's Our Band Could Be Your Life, Mascis says he thought Murph was about to beat up Barlow, so he figured he'd better do it himself. Barlow felt oddly vindicated: it proved Mascis had feelings. Murph just walked away.

years.h: Bug tops the UK indie chart
years.p: Recorded at Fort Apache in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Bug reaches No. 1 on the UK independent chart and stays 38 weeks; Freak Scene hits No. 4 there.
years.xp: J Mascis wrote the parts for Barlow and Murph and later called Bug his least favorite album: he liked some songs but not the vibe.

years.h: Lou Barlow screams Don't until he coughs blood
years.p: Barlow sings only the closing track on Bug, screaming one line over and over. He told Willamette Week he coughed up blood afterward, just throat irritation.

eras.title: Lou's out, Sire's in
eras.text: Mascis got rid of Barlow without quite saying so, and Barlow answered on record for years. Dinosaur Jr. signed to a major, turned mostly into J Mascis plus hired hands, and landed on the biggest alternative tours of the era.

q: I've never had such a visceral reaction to a cover version.
years.h: The Cure's Just Like Heaven, made loud
years.p: Recorded for a compilation, then kept because Dinosaur Jr. liked it too much to give away. [[Robert Smith|7d1a1624-784b-4f89-8ff9-b9b493cd059d]] says J Mascis's cassette changed how The Cure played the song live.

years.h: Lou Barlow thinks the band broke up. It hadn't
years.p: J Mascis and Murph come to Barlow's house with news Barlow hears as a breakup. He learns through the grapevine that Dinosaur Jr. is carrying on with a new bassist and a Warner deal.
years.xp: Barlow told Willamette Week that by the Bug sessions Mascis seemed sick of him and Murph and drained of enthusiasm. Barlow put his energy into [[Sebadoh|d98c8149-0c01-4151-93e1-48fdc3d5027f]].

years.h: The Wagon on Sub Pop, with members of Gumball
years.p: J Mascis and Murph cut the single with [[Don Fleming|deae7f43-894e-45f1-ae34-08bc0c921b82]] and Jay Spiegel of Gumball. [[Donna Dresch|a192432c-67e4-4eef-af43-25c6fb901a7b]] had played bass on an Australian tour.

years.h: Dinosaur Jr. signs to Sire Records
years.p: The major-label deal that had been lined up when Barlow was pushed out is signed.

years.h: Green Mind: J Mascis plays nearly everything
years.p: The major-label debut on Blanco y Negro/Sire. Murph barely plays; Mascis handles most drums himself and overdubs the rest.

years.h: Sebadoh III opens with The Freed Pig
years.p: Lou Barlow's first big Sebadoh album starts with a song about his treatment in Dinosaur Jr. and his anger at J Mascis.

years.h: Mike Johnson joins, and Nirvana opens
years.p: After Van Conner fills in, [[Mike Johnson|842226e0-fc89-468d-95c7-1e1cca0db944]] becomes the bassist. [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] supports Dinosaur Jr. on tour.

years.h: The Rollercoaster tour
years.p: Dinosaur Jr. joins [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]], [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]] and [[Blur|ba853904-ae25-4ebb-89d6-c44cfbd71bd2]] on a UK package tour.

years.h: Where You Been goes UK top 10
years.p: Murph back on most drums, Mike Johnson on bass and harmonies. Start Choppin' reaches the UK top 20 and Out There gets 120 Minutes rotation.

q: The worst touring experience I've ever had.
years.h: Lollapalooza: J Mascis's worst tour
years.p: Dinosaur Jr. plays the 1993 Lollapalooza. Mascis later told Magnet it was the worst touring experience he'd ever had.

years.h: Murph quits; J Mascis is the last original
years.p: After the Where You Been tour, Murph leaves. George Berz drums live; Murph joins [[The Lemonheads|58a53082-a629-4ff1-a44d-7492d6f6e8fb]] in 1995.

eras.title: A hit, then the Jenny Jones Show
eras.text: With Murph gone, Dinosaur Jr. was J Mascis in the studio plus Mike Johnson. It produced the band's biggest single, then fizzled on a label that barely promoted the last record.

years.h: Without a Sound and Feel the Pain
years.p: Feel the Pain is the band's biggest single: No. 4 on U.S. Alternative Airplay and No. 25 in the UK. In the Spike Jonze video, J Mascis and Mike Johnson play golf across New York.

years.h: Hand It Over barely gets promoted
years.p: J Mascis said the record had no hit single. Take a Run at the Sun reaches No. 53 in the UK on some editions.

years.h: Last stand: The Jenny Jones Show
years.p: Taped in New York, Dinosaur Jr. plays Never Bought It and Out There on the daytime talk show. It's the last performance before J Mascis retires the name.
years.xp: Low turnout on tour and little label push ended it. Mascis went solo as J Mascis + The Fog.

eras.title: Getting the tapes back
eras.text: Mascis took his time, then did the two things that made a reunion possible: he got the SST masters back, and he started showing up at Lou Barlow's gigs.

years.h: J Mascis + The Fog
years.p: Mascis puts out the first of two albums under the new name. He starts going to Sebadoh shows, and Lou Barlow realizes J doesn't hold a grudge.
years.xp: Barlow in 2005: once he saw Mascis wasn't avoiding him out of dislike, J became more human to him.

years.h: Two London shows as Asheton, Asheton, Mascis and Watt
years.p: J Mascis and [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] play Stooges songs in London with [[Ron Asheton|a10c8616-cdc3-4fd1-a0fa-bc35a6514168]] and [[Scott Asheton|8ff201f8-3b3f-40dd-a7f7-8d0a2184c62e]].

years.h: J Mascis wins back the first three albums from SST
years.p: Mascis regains the master rights and sets up reissues on Merge Records for early 2005.

years.h: The original trio returns on Craig Ferguson
years.p: J Mascis, Lou Barlow and Murph play The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson, their first time together since 1989. A European tour follows in June.
years.xp:
Asked what changed, Mascis said they chilled out; Barlow said they grew up.

In May, Barlow's mother organized an autism benefit at Smith College in Northampton, and Mascis and Barlow played a set as Deep Wound.

eras.title: The long second act
eras.text: The reunion was supposed to be a tour. It became two decades of records, more than the original lineup made the first time, from three people who still barely talk off stage.

years.h: Gear stolen outside a New York hotel
years.p: Much of Dinosaur Jr.'s equipment is taken from outside their hotel during a New York stop. The band also curates an All Tomorrow's Parties festival that year.

years.h: Beyond on Fat Possum
years.p: The first trio album of new songs since Bug, and Lou Barlow's first songwriting since You're Living All Over Me. It debuts at No. 69 and Pitchfork gives it 8.4.

years.h: Farm on Jagjaguwar, No. 29
years.p: Recorded at J Mascis's house, heavier and closer to Where You Been. It's the band's highest U.S. chart peak; they play Pieces on Jimmy Fallon two days after release.

years.h: I Bet on Sky
years.p: The third reunion album, on Jagjaguwar, to favorable reviews.

years.h: Lou Barlow: J Mascis and I aren't chatting
years.p: Barlow told NME that music is the glue between them. Murph says he's the go-between and the other two email once in a blue moon.

years.h: Give a Glimpse of What Yer Not
years.p: The fourth album since the reunion, on Jagjaguwar.
play: Give a Glimpse of What Yer Not

years.h: A 1994 song charts in Japan, thanks to TV
years.p: Over Your Shoulder from Without a Sound reaches No. 18 on Japan's Billboard chart, apparently because of its use on Gachinko Fight Club.

years.h: Sweep It Into Space, a year late
years.p: Album twelve was due in mid-2020 and held back by COVID-19. I Ran Away and Garden came out first.

years.h: Freakscene: The Story of Dinosaur Jr.
years.p: A feature documentary tells the band's story, from Deep Wound to the reunion.

years.h: There Near, album thirteen
years.p: Announced in June with the single Several Got Away, on Jagjaguwar.
